graph_and_ownership: Prepare/repack/validate scale values only during load, never capture; scale validation synchronizes.
Warm the Triton per-token quantization specialization and GEMM before capture.
Caller may pass per-token out/scales buffers and GEMM c; keep addresses alive for graph lifetime.
One zeroed lock workspace per concurrently executing stream/graph. It returns to zero only on successful completion. Do not reuse after failure until safely reset.
Upstream GEMM internally allocates FP32 reduction scratch: 4*SM_count*min(ceil(M/16)*16,64)*256 bytes. Graph private pools own captured scratch; no claim of allocator-free eager execution.
Native schemas declare mutation/aliasing. torch.compile/fake/functionalization integration is the consuming framework responsibility; raw CUDA graphs still require validation.
Replace original weights after repack; no package-owned full-model duplicate, no head/draft/sgl-kernel modifications.

numerical_policy.activation: Exact extracted CUDA Triton: FP32 absmax reduction with floor 1e-10, divide by127, libdevice.round (halfway away from zero) then int8. Finite inputs required.
numerical_policy.scale: Preserve upstream (s/s.max()*4096).round().int16().view(original_dtype), including FP16/BF16 arithmetic; input_global_scale=s.max().float()/4096. Reject nonfinite, zero maximum, or signed-int16 out-of-range conversion; negative scales are supported.
numerical_policy.weight_decode: Unchanged upstream uint4b8 nibble decode: integer range [-8,7].
numerical_policy.integer_accumulation: Local safety correction, not an upstream backport: IMMA sums remain int32, then signed-int64 multiply/add of the group scale; convert once per upstream slice with __ll2float_rn. No guessed carry representation or unchecked int32 multiplication remains in the supported path.

bound_derivation.production_requirement: For every layer, K%128=0, K>=256, N%64=0, N*K<=INT_MAX; each group has128 K entries. Bound includes all allowed layer shapes, not statistical activation assumptions.

numerical_policy.rounding_comparison: When upstream signed-int32 accumulation did not overflow, exact integer sum and final round-to-nearest FP32 conversion agree mathematically. Overflow inputs now compute the intended wide sum rather than wrapped signed integers. GPU proof pending.
